hypothesis: The bare failures come from the 7B losing track of its observations in the growing 36+-message chat, not from a lack of query vetoes. If every call is a fresh prompt (system prompt + a harness-rebuilt ledger of all answers, '?' for unasked rows, and the explicit list of still-unknown rows), then final guesses will stop contradicting rows the model itself observed (bare: 8 of 9 parsed guesses contradicted 2-11 observed rows) and repeated queries will vanish, all without the harness vetoing a circuit or overwriting any bit. Falsified if the observed-row contradiction rate stays above ~1/10.
behavior_changes: No running conversation: every self.llm call is [benchmark system prompt, one user message] built from env.history.

The user message says the game is in progress (N queries already made), lists every answer received in benchmark wording, shows per-circuit 8-row tables with '?', and lists the still-unknown rows per circuit with counts.

Query phase: a reply with no parseable query, or one that re-asks an already-answered row, is re-asked (up to 2 times, costs no query) with a note pointing back to the ledger. The wording varies on each re-ask because the seeded solver cache returns identical replies to identical prompts. No per-circuit cap; the model's query choice is never replaced.

Final phase: the same ledger plus the benchmark's last-turn prompt; the model is asked to fill every '?' from the task rules, keep the observed rows, and write 'A: <8 bits>', 'B: <8 bits>', 'C: <8 bits>'. The harness joins the model's three lines in benchmark order into <guess>; it falls back to the raw reply if any line is missing. Observed bits are NOT overwritten by the harness.
preserved_behaviors: Frozen solver: only self.llm; same system prompt and last-turn prompt from the benchmark.
Label-free: only env.query / env.history / env.format_answer / env.remaining / env.budget; no branching on inventory or instance index, no hard-coded tables.
The model writes every query and every bit of the final table; the harness never picks a query or substitutes a bit.
Full 18-query budget used; exactly one final guess.
verification: v1 (ledger only, generic wording): 0 crashes but broken. The model treated every fresh call as turn 1 ('Let's start by querying A(0,0,0)'), giving 16-18 repeats of one row. Identical re-ask prompts got identical cached replies, and only 3/10 episodes produced a parseable guess.

v2 ('MIDDLE of the game' framing, explicit unknown-row list, varied re-ask notes): 18 unique queries in all 10 episodes. The model's A:/B:/C: lines matched its observations, but it put them inside <guess>, so 9/10 failed to parse.
v3 (join the model's A:/B:/C: lines into the guess): ran check_b0r0_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b0r0g1.py. All 10 instances status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, queries_used=18, calls=19, 0 crashes.

Label-free audit of the v3 results: 0/10 final guesses contradict any row the model observed (bare: 8 of the 9 parsed guesses did, 0-11 rows each); 0 repeated queries (18/18 unique in every episode); no re-asks needed (19 calls = 18 queries + 1 final).

Query spread is unchanged from bare: A 8 / B 7-8 / C 2-3 in all 10 episodes, so C's table is almost entirely inferred. Some inferred rows look wrong from the rules alone: i128 has C=00000000 (a constant output, which the rules forbid), and in i128 B(1,1,1) was guessed 0 although every gate is AND/OR, so the circuit must be monotone.
risks: The ledger fixes transcription but NOT allocation: the model still enumerates A then B, so C is a near-blind guess. Exact 24-bit success is probably still rare; the circuits it fully queried should now be right. Combining this with a spread mechanism (or a rule-derived hint that 18 < 24 rows forces deduction) is the obvious next step but was deliberately left out to keep one causal lever.
Stateless prompts drop the model's own earlier reasoning (hypotheses about gate structure). That costs nothing while it enumerates, but could hurt a model that reasons adaptively.
The final assembly depends on the model following the 'A: <8 bits>' line format; when it doesn't, it falls back to the raw reply (the old bare behavior).
Inferred '?' rows can violate the rules (constant circuit, non-monotone with AND/OR-only inventory); nothing in this harness checks that.
